name: Other tabs and windows content
plain: A page cannot see what other tabs show, only whether its own tab is visible.
meaning: Same-origin policy and site isolation block it. Proxies: Page Visibility and focus say if this tab is hidden, BroadcastChannel talks to same-origin tabs, and Window Management lists screens (prompt). Number of open tabs is unknown.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: document.visibilityState
fields.range: visible or hidden for this tab

limits.headline: Can't see what other tabs or windows show
limits.user_action: Nothing. Pages have no way to ask for this
can: Tell if its own tab is visible or hidden
Talk to other tabs of the same site
List your screens after you allow it in Chrome or Edge
Pause itself when the tab is in the background
cannot: Count how many tabs you have open
See titles or links of other tabs

story.what_it_is: A page cannot see what your other tabs show. It can only tell whether its own tab is visible.

marketing.name: Site Isolation
marketing.pitch: Chrome puts pages from different sites in separate processes so one site cannot read another's data.

marketing.name: Page Visibility API
marketing.pitch: Docs describe how a page learns whether its own tab is visible.

story.for_you: Your banking tab cannot be read by a shopping tab, even if they are open side by side. A site can only tell whether you are looking at it or have switched away.
story.for_makers: Reading other tabs would expose logins and private data, so browsers wall them off. Sites can still see their own tab's visibility to pause video or count attention time. Same-site tabs can talk to each other.

use_cases.example: A video site pauses playback when you switch tabs, but cannot see what you switched to.
A browser game pauses when the tab is hidden and has no view of other tabs.
An ad vendor measures if its ad was in view and cannot see other tabs.
A malicious page wanted to read your bank tab and is blocked by site isolation.
A web email app syncs across its own open tabs using a shared channel.
An exam site detects that you left its tab and records that, but not what you opened.
A news site counts how long its tab was visible to measure attention.

risks: Can still see that you switched away

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
